newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam jails golf course protesters.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam jails golf course protesters.

text.p: Vietnam has jailed four people for involvement in violent clashes between police and villagers over the construction of a luxury golf-course on the outskirts of Hanoi.
Court officials said on Friday the three men and one woman had been sentenced to prison terms of between three and five years on charges of opposing police officers on duty.
The four were among some 1,000 local people involved in clashes in March and May with hundreds of police who were trying to evict them from farming land earmarked for the course.

Villagers at the Kim No commune told Reuters that one woman had died and scores of others had been injured in violence on May 13 which erupted when police began ripping rice plants from the field being appropriated.
The woman was said to have drowned after falling into a water-hole during the melee.
A police journal report on the incident did not mention the death but said security officials had been injured and illegally held by "extremists" and then forced to write confessions.
The trial was held last week.
Another woman, Pham Thi Oanh, was jailed for 12 months and a sixth person given a suspended sentence at an earlier hearing.
The planned golf course is part of a $177 million project involving South Korea's Daewoo Group.
